key_insight: Stochastically selecting a subset of patch-aligned features from a foundation model (BLIP2) removes heavy redundancy (≈90%) caused by self-attention, and training policies on fewer patches improves out-of-distribution generalization for end-to-end driving — see less, drive better.
problem_solved: High redundancy in patch-level foundation-model features causes inefficient, overfit end-to-end driving policies that generalize poorly to OOD scenarios; the paper addresses how to reduce redundancy and improve robustness.
method: Quantify redundancy in BLIP2 patch features via PCA and cross-patch similarity (≈90% redundancy observed).
Introduce Stochastic Patch Selection: randomly sample/drop patch-aligned features during training so the policy cannot rely on redundant cross-patch encodings.
Train end-to-end driving policies on reduced patch sets and evaluate on OOD benchmarks to demonstrate improved robustness and efficiency.
impact: Reducing redundant visual inputs yields more robust, generalizable driving policies and lowers input dimensionality and compute, benefiting practitioners building vision-to-control systems that must operate safely in novel environments.

paper_title: See Less, Drive Better: Generalizable End-to-End Autonomous Driving via Foundation Models Stochastic Patch Selection
paper_authors: Amir Mallak, Erfan Aasi, Shiva Sreeram, Tsun-Hsuan Wang, Daniela Rus
